What Is Automotive Powder Coating?

Automotive powder coating is a dry finishing process in which electrostatically charged powder is sprayed onto metal vehicle parts, then heated in an oven until it melts and cures into a hard, even coating. It protects bare metal from rust, chips and everyday wear.

The finish is made from thermoset powder, which cures with heat instead of drying like liquid paint. At a cure temperature of 180 to 200 °C, the powder flows, bonds to the metal and hardens into one continuous layer without runs or drips. That makes it a dependable corrosion-resistant automotive coating for parts that face grit, moisture and impact, such as frames, brackets, suspension arms and underbody components. That is why vehicle powder coating is common on trucks and trailers that see winter road salt.

Typical customers include builders of custom motorcycles, owners of trucks and trailers, and shops that send out metal parts for finishing. If your project needs custom car parts powder coating, our [powder coating services](/services) cover it from intake to handoff. Good auto parts powder coating also depends on the work done before the powder goes on, so we plan every job from the bare metal up.
Our Automotive Powder Coating Process

Our automotive powder coating process has six stages: intake and inspection, cleaning and pretreatment, masking, powder application, oven curing and final inspection. Each stage is documented so repeat orders match the first batch. The same controls support our [industrial powder coating](/services/industrial-powder-coating) work.
Step 1 – Intake and Inspection

We check each part for heavy rust, old coatings, weld quality and damage, then confirm the finish you want for your automotive powder coating order. We also decide how to hang the part so every surface can be reached.
Step 2 – Cleaning and Pretreatment
Parts are washed and pretreated so the powder bonds to clean metal. Skipping this stage is a common reason rust protection for car parts fails early.
Step 3 – Masking and Plugging

Threads, bearing surfaces and mounting holes are protected before coating. Masking and plugging keep bolts turning and parts fitting, which matters on any valve cover powder coating or engine bracket powder coating order.
Step 4 – Electrostatic Powder Application
Charged powder is sprayed onto the grounded part, so it wraps around tubes, corners and recesses. Electrostatic powder application gives an even film across a complex frame.
Step 5 – Oven Curing

The part moves into the curing oven, where automotive powder coating reaches temperature and hardens. Cure time depends on the powder and the mass of the part, so a heavy chassis is planned differently from a small bracket.
Step 6 – Final Inspection and Handoff

We inspect the cured finish for coverage, adhesion and appearance. Typical orders are ready within 48 hours, and larger batch powder coating jobs are scheduled when we quote. We receive parts Monday to Friday, 7 AM to 5 PM.
Our automotive powder coating services schedule each stage so parts never wait between steps, and for car powder coating on a deadline, tell us your date at quote.

Choose from gloss, satin, matte and textured finishes in a wide range of colours. We confirm the powder type, colour code and film thickness at quote, so the finish suits the part, the metal and how it will be used.

Quality Standards for Automotive Powder Coating

Our automotive powder coating follows recognized standards: ASTM D3359 for adhesion, ASTM D7091 for dry film thickness and ASTM B117 for salt spray resistance. Koojo is certified through the Absolute Bureau of Certification, and test reports are available on request.

Quality starts at intake and ends at handoff. After curing, a good finish looks even in colour and gloss, with no thin spots, runs or bare edges. We flag any concern with you before parts leave the shop.

An ASTM D3359 adhesion test checks that the coating bonds to the metal. Dry film thickness readings confirm the coating is neither too thin to protect nor too thick to fit. The ASTM B117 salt spray test measures corrosion resistance in a controlled chamber. It is a comparison tool rather than a promise of real-world life, so we explain what results mean for your parts.

Batch inspection means each load is checked before parts leave the shop, which keeps repeat orders consistent and adds road salt protection you can rely on. Careful vehicle powder coating also depends on clean prep and correct curing, so every order follows the same documented steps. See our [certification](/certification) page for details.

Automotive Powder Coating FAQs

Short answer: we coat steel, aluminum and cast car parts in batches, with fast turnaround on typical orders. These answers cover size, timing, rust, fit and logistics so you know what to expect before you book your order. Ask us anything else before you send parts.

blocks.q: What size of car parts can you coat?
blocks.a: Our automotive powder coating handles everything from small brackets to full frames. Our capabilities page lists 6,000 lb capacity, so send dimensions and weight with your quote and we will confirm the fit.

blocks.q: How long does automotive powder coating take?
blocks.a: Typical orders follow our 48-hour turnaround. Large, heavy or high-volume jobs are scheduled at quote, and we receive parts Monday to Friday, 7 AM to 5 PM.

blocks.q: Can you coat parts with rust or old paint?
blocks.a: Yes, but heavy rust and old coatings must come off before powder goes on. Tell us the condition when you quote, and see our [powder coat stripping and recoating](/services/restoration-recoating) service for parts that need full removal.

blocks.q: Will bolts and threads still fit after coating?
blocks.a: Yes, when we mask them. We plug threaded holes and protect mounting faces, and we confirm film thickness on tight-tolerance parts. Flag fit-critical areas on your quote.

blocks.q: What finish suits winter driving and road salt?
blocks.a: Protection depends on correct prep, the right powder and a full cure more than on colour or gloss. Tell us how the part is used, and we will recommend a powder for vehicle powder coating on trucks and cars driven through winter.

blocks.q: Do you offer pickup and delivery?
blocks.a: For auto parts powder coating, pickup and delivery details are confirmed at quote based on your location and parts. You can also drop parts off at 10874 Steeles Ave E, Milton, during opening hours.
